attributes.name: user_pf_options
attributes.description: User-defined power flow options. Custom settings for power flow calculations.

attributes.name: res_cost
attributes.description: Optimal power flow total cost result. This is the objective function value of the OPF optimization, representing the total cost of generation/operation based on the defined cost functions for controllable elements (generators, external grids, loads, etc.).

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Total optimized cost calculated as the sum of all individual element costs: Σ[f_i(P_i)] for all controllable elements i (ext_grid, gen, sgen, load, dcline, storage), where f_i is the cost function (polynomial or piecewise linear) defined for element i. Only includes costs for elements that are controllable and participate in the OPF optimization.

attributes.name: _ppc
attributes.description: Internal PYPOWER case format data structure. This is a private attribute that stores the network data converted to PYPOWER/MATPOWER format for power flow calculations. Users should not directly modify this structure.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: PYPOWER case file format version (typically '2')

parameters.name: baseMVA
parameters.description: System base power for per-unit calculations. Typically set to net.sn_mva (default 1 MVA)

parameters.name: bus
parameters.description: Bus data matrix in PYPOWER format. Shape: (n_bus, 13). Columns: bus_i, type, Pd, Qd, Gs, Bs, area, Vm, Va, baseKV, zone, Vmax, Vmin. Contains voltage levels, power injections, and bus constraints

parameters.name: gen
parameters.description: Generator data matrix in PYPOWER format. Shape: (n_gen, 21). Columns: bus, Pg, Qg, Qmax, Qmin, Vg, mBase, status, Pmax, Pmin, etc. Contains generator active/reactive power outputs and constraints

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Branch (line/transformer) data matrix in PYPOWER format. Shape: (n_branch, 13). Columns: fbus, tbus, r, x, b, rateA, rateB, rateC, ratio, angle, status, angmin, angmax. Contains impedance, ratings, and branch status

parameters.name: gencost
parameters.description: Generator cost data matrix for OPF. Shape: (n_gen, variable). Contains polynomial or piecewise linear cost function coefficients. Only present after OPF setup

parameters.name: bus_name
parameters.description: Array of bus names corresponding to bus matrix rows

parameters.name: success
parameters.description: Power flow convergence flag. True if the last calculation converged successfully

parameters.name: iterations
parameters.description: Number of iterations taken by the power flow solver

parameters.name: et
parameters.description: Elapsed time for the power flow calculation

parameters.name: internal
parameters.description: Pandapower-specific internal data including reference bus indices, ordering information, and auxiliary bus mappings. Used for result extraction and network topology handling

parameters.name: bus_pq
parameters.description: Extended bus data with additional PQ injection information. Used internally for more detailed power flow calculations

parameters.name: gen_controllable
parameters.description: Boolean array indicating which generators are controllable in OPF. Only present during OPF calculations

attributes.name: _pd2ppc_lookups
attributes.description: Lookup tables mapping pandapower element indices to PYPOWER matrix row indices. This internal structure is essential for bidirectional conversion between pandapower's DataFrame-based format and PYPOWER's matrix-based format. Used during result extraction to map calculation results back to pandapower tables.

parameters.name: bus
parameters.description: Bus index mapping array. Maps pandapower bus indices to PYPOWER ppc['bus'] row indices. Shape: (n_bus,). Entry bus[i] gives the row index in ppc['bus'] for pandapower bus i. Value of -1 indicates the bus is out of service

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: Branch element mapping dictionary. Contains separate arrays for each branch element type (line, trafo, trafo3w, impedance, switch). Each array maps pandapower element indices to ppc['branch'] row indices

parameters.name: branch['line']
parameters.description: Line index mapping. Maps net.line indices to their corresponding rows in ppc['branch']. Shape: (n_line,)

parameters.name: branch['trafo']
parameters.description: Two-winding transformer index mapping. Maps net.trafo indices to ppc['branch'] rows. Shape: (n_trafo,)

parameters.name: branch['trafo3w']
parameters.description: Three-winding transformer mapping. Contains three arrays ('hv', 'mv', 'lv') for the three internal branches representing each trafo3w element in ppc['branch']

parameters.name: branch['impedance']
parameters.description: Impedance element index mapping. Maps net.impedance indices to ppc['branch'] rows. Shape: (n_impedance,)

parameters.name: branch['switch']
parameters.description: Switch element index mapping (only for closed switches modeled as branches). Maps net.switch indices to ppc['branch'] rows

parameters.name: gen
parameters.description: Generator element mapping dictionary. Contains separate arrays for each generator type (gen, sgen, ext_grid, storage, etc.). Maps pandapower generator indices to ppc['gen'] row indices

parameters.name: gen['gen']
parameters.description: Synchronous generator index mapping. Maps net.gen indices to ppc['gen'] rows. Shape: (n_gen,)

parameters.name: gen['sgen']
parameters.description: Static generator index mapping. Maps net.sgen indices to ppc['gen'] rows. Shape: (n_sgen,)

parameters.name: gen['ext_grid']
parameters.description: External grid index mapping. Maps net.ext_grid indices to ppc['gen'] rows (slack generators). Shape: (n_ext_grid,)

parameters.name: gen['storage']
parameters.description: Storage element index mapping. Maps net.storage indices to ppc['gen'] rows. Shape: (n_storage,)

parameters.name: bus_lookup
parameters.description: Auxiliary bus lookup dictionary. Contains mappings for auxiliary buses created internally (e.g., for three-winding transformers, switches). Keys are pandapower element types, values are arrays of auxiliary bus indices

parameters.name: ext_grid
parameters.description: Direct external grid mapping (redundant with gen['ext_grid']). Maps net.ext_grid indices to their representation. Shape: (n_ext_grid,)

attributes.name: protection
attributes.description: Protection device data table.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: Protection device object instance. Stores the actual Python protection relay object containing the protection logic, settings, and methods. Similar to controller objects, this allows complex protection behavior to be encapsulated in custom classes.

parameters.description: Type of the bus. "n" - node, "b" - busbar, "m" - muff

parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: grid region

parameters.name: max_vm_pu
parameters.description: Maximum bus voltage in p.u. - necessary for OPF

parameters.description: Minimum bus voltage in p.u. - necessary for OPF

parameters.description: busbar coordinates to plot the bus with multiple points. coords is typically a list of tuples (start and endpoint of the busbar) - Example: [(x1, y1), (x2, y2)]

functions.description: Adds several dc buses in table net["bus_dc"] at once.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: The pandapower network in which the element is created

parameters.name: nr_buses_dc
parameters.description: The number of dc buses that is created

parameters.name: vn_kv
parameters.description: The grid voltage level.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Force specified IDs if available. If None, the indices higher than the highest already existing index are selected.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the name for this dc bus

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Type of the dc bus. "n" - auxilary node, "b" - busbar, "m" - muff

parameters.name: geodata
parameters.type: (x,y)-tuple or list of tuples with length == nr_buses_dc
parameters.description: coordinates used for plotting

parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: grid region

parameters.name: in_service
parameters.description: True for in_service or False for out of service

parameters.name: max_vm_pu
parameters.description: Maximum bus voltage in p.u. - necessary for OPF

parameters.name: min_vm_pu
parameters.description: Minimum bus voltage in p.u. - necessary for OPF

parameters.name: coords
parameters.description: busbar coordinates to plot the dc bus with multiple points. coords is typically a list of tuples (start and endpoint of the busbar) - Example for 3 dc buses: [[(x11, y11), (x12, y12)], [(x21, y21), (x22, y22)], [(x31, y31), (x32, y32)]]

return_info.description: **index** (int) - The unique indices ID of the created elements

examples:
import pandapower as pp
net = pp.create_empty_network()
bus_ids = pp.create_buses_dc(net, nr_buses_dc=2, vn_kv=[20., 20.], name=["bus1","bus2"])

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Force a specified ID if it is available. If None, the index one higher than the highest already existing index is selected.

parameters.description: The geodata of the line. The first element should be the coordinates of from_bus and the last should be the coordinates of to_bus. The points in the middle represent the bending points of the line

parameters.description: derating factor: maximum current of line in relation to nominal current of line (from 0 to 1)

parameters.name: parallel

parameters.name: in_service

parameters.name: max_loading_percent

parameters.description: temperature coefficient of resistance: R(T) = R(T_0) * (1 + alpha * (T - T_0))

parameters.name: temperature_degree_celsius
parameters.description: line temperature for which line resistance is adjusted

return_info.description: **index** (int) - The unique ID of the created line

functions.description: Adds a switch in the net["switch"] table.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: The net within which this switch should be created

parameters.name: bus
parameters.description: The bus that the switch is connected to

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: index of the element: bus id if et == "b", line id if et == "l", trafo id if et == "t"

parameters.name: et
parameters.description: (string) element type: "l" = switch between bus and line, "t" = switch between bus and transformer, "t3" = switch between bus and transformer3w, "b" = switch between two buses

parameters.name: closed
parameters.description: switch position: False = open, True = closed

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: indicates the type of switch: "LS" = Load Switch, "CB" = Circuit Breaker, "LBS" = Load Break Switch or "DS" = Disconnecting Switch

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name for this switch

parameters.name: z_ohm
parameters.description: indicates the resistance of the switch, which has effect only on bus-bus switches, if sets to 0, the buses will be fused like before, if larger than 0 a branch will be created for the switch which has also effects on the bus mapping

parameters.name: in_ka
parameters.description: maximum current that the switch can carry normal operating conditions without tripping

return_info.description: **sid** - The unique switch_id of the created switch

switch_id = pp.create_switch(net, bus=b1, element=b2, et="b", closed=True)

parameters.description: Model this sgen as a current source during short- circuit calculations; useful in some cases, for example the simulation of full- size converters per IEC 60909-0:2016.

parameters.name: max_ik_ka
parameters.description: the highest instantaneous short-circuit value in case of a three-phase short-circuit (provided by the manufacturer). Relevant if the generator_type is "async_doubly_fed".

parameters.name: kappa
parameters.description: the factor for the calculation of the peak short-circuit current, referred to the high-voltage side (provided by the manufacturer). Relevant if the generator_type is "async_doubly_fed". If the superposition method is used (use_pre_fault_voltage=True), this parameter is used to pass through the max. current limit of the machine in p.u.

parameters.name: lrc_pu
parameters.description: locked rotor current in relation to the rated generator current. Relevant if the generator_type is "async".

return_info.description: **index** (int) - The unique ID of the created sgen

parameters.description: The active power of the static generator : Phase B

parameters.name: p_c_mw
parameters.description: The active power of the static generator : Phase C

parameters.name: q_a_mvar

parameters.description: The reactive power of the sgen : Phase B

functions.description: Creates a two-winding transformer in table net.trafo. The trafo parameters are defined through the standard type library.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: the net within this transformer should be created

parameters.name: hv_bus
parameters.description: the bus on the high-voltage side on which the transformer will be connected to

parameters.name: lv_bus
parameters.description: τhe bus on the low-voltage side on which the transformer will be connected to

parameters.name: std_type
parameters.description: τhe used standard type from the standard type library

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: a custom name for this transformer

parameters.name: tap_pos
parameters.description: current tap position of the transformer. Defaults to the medium position (tap_neutral)

parameters.name: in_service
parameters.description: True for in_service or False for out of service

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: force a specified ID if it is available. If None, the index one higher than the highest already existing index is selected

parameters.name: max_loading_percent
parameters.description: maximum current loading (only needed for OPF)

parameters.name: parallel
parameters.description: number of parallel transformers

parameters.name: df
parameters.description: derating factor: maximum current of transformer in relation to nominal current of transformer (from 0 to 1)

parameters.name: tap_changer_type
parameters.description: specifies the phase shifter type ("Ratio", "Symmetrical", "Ideal", "Tabular", None: no tap changer)

parameters.name: tap_dependency_table
parameters.description: True if transformer parameters (voltage ratio, angle, impedance) must be adjusted dependent on the tap position of the transformer. Requires the additional column "id_characteristic_table". The function pandapower.control.trafo_characteristic_table_diagnostic can be used for sanity checks. The function pandapower.control.create_trafo_characteristic_object can be used to create SplineCharacteristic objects in the net.trafo_characteristic_spline table and add the additional column "id_characteristic_spline" to set up the reference to the spline characteristics.

parameters.name: id_characteristic_table
parameters.description: references the index of the characteristic from the lookup table net.trafo_characteristic_table

parameters.name: pt_percent
parameters.description: zero sequence relative short-circuit voltage

parameters.name: xn_ohm
parameters.description: impedance of the grounding reactor (Z_N) for short circuit calculation

parameters.name: tap2_pos
parameters.description: current tap position of the second tap changer of the transformer. Defaults to the medium position (tap2_neutral)

return_info.description: **index** (int) - the unique ID of the created transformer

examples:
import pandapower as pp

hv_bus = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.0)

trafo_id = pp.create_transformer(net, hv_bus=hv_bus, lv_bus=lv_bus, std_type="0.4 MVA 20/0.4 kV")

functions.description: Creates a shunt element.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: the pandapower network in which the element is created

parameters.name: bus
parameters.description: index of the bus the shunt is connected to

parameters.name: q_mvar
parameters.description: shunt reactive power in MVAr at v = 1.0 p.u. per step

parameters.name: p_mw
parameters.description: shunt active power in MW at v = 1.0 p.u. per step

parameters.name: vn_kv
parameters.description: rated voltage of the shunt. Defaults to rated voltage of connected bus, since this value is mandatory for powerflow calculations. If it is set to NaN it will be replaced by the bus vn_kv during power flow

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: step of shunt with which power values are multiplied

parameters.name: max_step
parameters.description: maximum allowed step of shunt

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: element name

parameters.name: step_dependency_table
parameters.description: True if shunt parameters (p_mw, q_mvar) must be adjusted dependent on the step of the shunt. Requires the additional column "id_characteristic_table". The function pandapower.control.shunt_characteristic_table_diagnostic can be used for sanity checks. The function pandapower.control.create_shunt_characteristic_object can be used to create SplineCharacteristic objects in the net.shunt_characteristic_spline table and add the additional column "id_characteristic_spline" to set up the reference to the spline characteristics.

parameters.name: id_characteristic_table
parameters.description: references the index of the characteristic from the lookup table net.shunt_characteristic_table

parameters.name: in_service
parameters.description: True for in_service or False for out of service

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: force a specified ID if it is available. If None, the index one higher than the highest already existing index is selected.

return_info.description: **index** (int) - the unique ID of the created shunt

examples:
import pandapower as pp
net = pp.create_empty_network()
bus = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.0)
shunt_id = pp.create_shunt(net, bus=bus, q_mvar=0.5, p_mw=0)

parameters.description: The zero-sequence imaginary part of the impedance from 'from_bus' to 'to_bus' in per unit. Default is None.

parameters.name: bf_pu

parameters.name: bt_pu
parameters.description: Susceptance at the 'to_bus' in per unit. Defaults to `bf_pu`.

parameters.name: gf0_pu
parameters.description: The zero-sequence conductance at the 'from_bus' in per unit. Default is None.

parameters.name: bf0_pu
parameters.description: The zero-sequence susceptance at the 'from_bus' in per unit. Default is None.

parameters.name: gt0_pu
parameters.description: The zero-sequence conductance at the 'to_bus' in per unit. Defaults to `gf0_pu`.

parameters.name: bt0_pu
parameters.description: The zero-sequence susceptance at the 'to_bus' in per unit. Defaults to `bf0_pu`.

parameters.name: kwargs
parameters.description: Additional arguments (for additional columns in net.impedance table).

functions.name: create_measurement
functions.signature: pandapower.create_measurement(net, meas_type, element_type, value, std_dev, element, side=None, check_existing=False, index=None, name=None, **kwargs)
functions.description: Creates a measurement, which is used by the estimation module. Possible types of measurements are: v, p, q, i, va, ia

parameters.name: meas_type
parameters.description: Type of measurement. "v", "p", "q", "i", "va" and "ia" are possible

parameters.name: element_type
parameters.description: Clarifies which element is measured. "bus", "line", "trafo", "trafo3w", "load", "gen", "sgen", "shunt", "ward", "xward" and "ext_grid" are possible

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Measurement value. Units are "MW" for P, "MVAr" for Q, "p.u." for V, "kA" for I. Bus power measurement is in load reference system, which is consistent to the rest of pandapower.

parameters.name: std_dev
parameters.description: Standard deviation in the same unit as the measurement

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: Index of the measured element

parameters.name: side
parameters.description: Only used for measured lines or transformers. Side defines at which end of the branch the measurement is gathered. For lines this may be "from", "to" to denote the side with the from_bus or to_bus. It can also be the index of the from_bus or to_bus. For transformers, it can be "hv", "mv" or "lv" or the corresponding bus index, respectively.

parameters.name: check_existing
parameters.description: Check for and replace existing measurements for this bus, type and element_type. Set it to False for performance improvements which can cause unsafe behavior.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Index of the measurement in the measurement table. Should not exist already.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of measurement

return_info.description: **index** (int) - Index of the created measurement EXAMPLES: 2 MW load measurement with 0.05 MW standard deviation on bus 0: create_measurement(net, "p", "bus", 0, 2., 0.05.) 4.5 MVar line measurement with 0.1 MVAr standard deviation on the "to_bus" side of line 2: create_measurement(net, "q", "line", 2, 4.5, 0.1, "to")

functions.name: change_std_type
functions.description: Changes the type of a given element in pandapower. Changes only parameter that are given for the type.

parameters.description: pandapower network

parameters.name: eid
parameters.description: element index (either line or transformer index)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: name of the new standard type

parameters.description: type of element ("line" or "trafo")

functions.name: parameter_from_std_type

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: pandapower network

parameters.name: parameter
parameters.description: name of parameter as string

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: type of element ("line" or "trafo")

parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: fill-value that is assigned to all lines/trafos without a value for the parameter, either because the line/trafo has no type or because the type does not have a value for the parameter

functions.name: find_std_type_by_parameter
functions.description: Searches for a std_type that fits all values given in the data dictionary with the margin of epsilon.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: pandapower network

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: dictionary of standard type parameters

parameters.name: element

functions.name: runpp
functions.signature: pandapower.runpp(net, algorithm='nr', calculate_voltage_angles=True, init='auto', max_iteration='auto', tolerance_mva=1e-08, trafo_model='t', trafo_loading='current', enforce_q_lims=False, check_connectivity=True, voltage_depend_loads=True, consider_line_temperature=False, run_control=False, distributed_slack=False, tdpf=False, tdpf_delay_s=None, **kwargs)
functions.description: Runs a power flow

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: The pandapower format network

parameters.name: algorithm
parameters.description: algorithm that is used to solve the power flow problem. The following algorithms are available: - "nr" Newton-Raphson (pypower implementation with numba accelerations) - "iwamoto_nr" Newton-Raphson with Iwamoto multiplier (maybe slower than NR but more robust) - "bfsw" backward/forward sweep (specially suited for radial and weakly-meshed networks) - "gs" gauss-seidel (pypower implementation) - "fdbx" fast-decoupled (pypower implementation) - "fdxb" fast-decoupled (pypower implementation)

parameters.name: calculate_voltage_angles
parameters.description: consider voltage angles in loadflow calculation If True, voltage angles of ext_grids and transformer shifts are considered in the loadflow calculation. Considering the voltage angles is only necessary in meshed networks that are usually found in higher voltage levels. calculate_voltage_angles in "auto" mode defaults to: - True, if the network voltage level is above 70 kV - False otherwise The network voltage level is defined as the maximum rated voltage of any bus in the network that is connected to a line.

parameters.name: init
parameters.description: initialization method of the loadflow pandapower supports four methods for initializing the loadflow: - "auto" - init defaults to "dc" if calculate_voltage_angles is True or "flat" otherwise - "flat"- flat start with voltage of 1.0pu and angle of 0° at all PQ-buses and 0° for PV buses as initial solution, the slack bus is initialized with the values provided in net["ext_grid"] - "dc" - initial DC loadflow before the AC loadflow. The results of the DC loadflow are used as initial solution for the AC loadflow. Note that the DC loadflow only calculates voltage angles at PQ and PV buses, voltage magnitudes are still flat started. - "results" - voltage vector of last loadflow from net.res_bus is used as initial solution. This can be useful to accelerate convergence in iterative loadflows like time series calculations. Considering the voltage angles might lead to non-convergence of the power flow in flat start. That is why in "auto" mode, init defaults to "dc" if calculate_voltage_angles is True or "flat" otherwise

parameters.name: max_iteration
parameters.description: maximum number of iterations carried out in the power flow algorithm. In "auto" mode, the default value depends on the power flow solver: - 10 for "nr" - 100 for "bfsw" - 1000 for "gs" - 30 for "fdbx" - 30 for "fdxb" - 30 for "nr" with "tdpf"

parameters.name: tolerance_mva
parameters.description: loadflow termination condition referring to P / Q mismatch of node power in MVA

parameters.name: trafo_model
parameters.description: transformer equivalent circuit model pandapower provides two equivalent circuit models for the transformer: - "t" - transformer is modeled as equivalent with the T-model. - "pi" - transformer is modeled as equivalent PI-model. This is not recommended, since it is less exact than the T-model. It is only recommended for valdiation with other software that uses the pi-model.

parameters.name: trafo_loading
parameters.description: mode of calculation for transformer loading Transformer loading can be calculated relative to the rated current or the rated power. In both cases the overall transformer loading is defined as the maximum loading on the two sides of the transformer. - "current"- transformer loading is given as ratio of current flow and rated current of the transformer. This is the recommended setting, since thermal as well as magnetic effects in the transformer depend on the current. - "power" - transformer loading is given as ratio of apparent power flow to the rated apparent power of the transformer.

parameters.name: enforce_q_lims
parameters.description: respect generator reactive power limits If True, the reactive power limits in net.gen.max_q_mvar/min_q_mvar are respected in the loadflow. This is done by running a second loadflow if reactive power limits are violated at any generator, so that the runtime for the loadflow will increase if reactive power has to be curtailed.

parameters.name: check_connectivity
parameters.description: Perform an extra connectivity test after the conversion from pandapower to PYPOWER If True, an extra connectivity test based on SciPy Compressed Sparse Graph Routines is perfomed. If check finds unsupplied buses, they are set out of service in the ppc

parameters.name: voltage_depend_loads
parameters.description: consideration of voltage-dependent loads. If False, net.load.const_z_percent and net.load.const_i_percent are not considered, i.e. net.load.p_mw and net.load.q_mvar are considered as constant-power loads.

parameters.name: consider_line_temperature
parameters.description: adjustment of line impedance based on provided line temperature. If True, net.line must contain a column "temperature_degree_celsius". The temperature dependency coefficient alpha must be provided in the net.line.alpha column, otherwise the default value of 0.004 is used

parameters.name: distributed_slack
parameters.description: Distribute slack power according to contribution factor weights for external grids and generators.

parameters.name: tdpf
parameters.description: Temperature Dependent Power Flow (TDPF). If True, line temperature is calculated based on the TDPF parameters in net.line table.

parameters.name: tdpf_delay_s
parameters.description: TDPF parameter, specifies the time delay in s to consider thermal inertia of conductors.

examples:
import pandapower as pp
net = pp.create_empty_network()
b1 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.0)
b2 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.0)
pp.create_ext_grid(net, bus=b1)
pp.create_line(net, from_bus=b1, to_bus=b2, length_km=1.0, std_type="NAYY 4x50 SE")
pp.create_load(net, bus=b2, p_mw=0.1, q_mvar=0.05)
pp.runpp(net)

functions.description: Runs PANDAPOWER DC Flow

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: The pandapower format network

parameters.name: trafo_model
parameters.description: transformer equivalent circuit model pandapower provides two equivalent circuit models for the transformer: - "t" - transformer is modeled as equivalent with the T-model. This is consistent with PowerFactory and is also more accurate than the PI-model. We recommend using this transformer model. - "pi" - transformer is modeled as equivalent PI-model. This is consistent with Sincal, but the method is questionable since the transformer is physically T-shaped. We therefore recommend the use of the T-model.

parameters.name: trafo_loading
parameters.description: mode of calculation for transformer loading Transformer loading can be calculated relative to the rated current or the rated power. In both cases the overall transformer loading is defined as the maximum loading on the two sides of the transformer. - "current"- transformer loading is given as ratio of current flow and rated current of the transformer. This is the recommended setting, since thermal as well as magnetic effects in the transformer depend on the current. - "power" - transformer loading is given as ratio of apparent power flow to the rated apparent power of the transformer.

parameters.name: check_connectivity
parameters.description: Perform an extra connectivity test after the conversion from pandapower to PYPOWER If true, an extra connectivity test based on SciPy Compressed Sparse Graph Routines is perfomed. If check finds unsupplied buses, they are put out of service in the PYPOWER matrix

parameters.name: switch_rx_ratio
parameters.description: rx_ratio of bus-bus-switches. If the impedance of switches defined in net.switch.z_ohm is zero, buses connected by a closed bus-bus switch are fused to model an ideal bus. Closed bus-bus switches, whose impedance z_ohm is not zero, are modelled as branches with resistance and reactance according to net.switch.z_ohm and switch_rx_ratio.

parameters.name: trafo3w_losses

functions.description: Obtain either loading (N-0) or max. loading (N-0 and all N-1 cases), and min/max bus voltage magnitude. The variable "temperature_degree_celsius" can be used in addition to "loading_percent" to obtain max. temperature. In the returned dictionary, the variable "loading_percent" represents the loading in N-0 case, "max_loading_percent" and "min_loading_percent" represent highest and lowest observed loading_percent among all calculated N-1 cases. The same convention applies to "temperature_degree_celsius" when applicable. This function can be passed through to pandapower.timeseries.run_timeseries as the run_control_fct argument.

parameters.description: dict options for power flow calculation in N-1 cases

parameters.name: write_to_net
parameters.description: bool whether to write the results of contingency analysis to net (in "res_" tables). The results will be written for the following additional variables: table res_bus with columns "max_vm_pu", "min_vm_pu", tables res_line, res_trafo, res_trafo3w with columns "max_loading_percent", "min_loading_percent", "causes_overloading", "cause_element", "cause_index", table res_line with columns "max_temperature_degree_celsius", "min_temperature_degree_celsius" (if "tdpf" set to True) "causes_overloading": does this element, when defining the N-1 case, cause overloading of other elements? the overloading is defined by net.line["max_loading_percent_nminus1"] (if set) or net.line["max_loading_percent"] "cause_element": element ("line", "trafo", "trafo3w") that causes max. loading of this element "cause_index": index of the element ("line", "trafo", "trafo3w") that causes max. loading of this element

return_info.description: ------- **contingency_results** - dict dict of arrays per element for index, min/max result

functions.name: get_equivalent
functions.signature: pandapower.grid_equivalents.get_equivalent(net, eq_type, boundary_buses, internal_buses, return_internal=True, show_computing_time=False, ward_type='ward_injection', adapt_va_degree=False, calculate_voltage_angles=True, allow_net_change_for_convergence=False, runpp_fct=<function _runpp_except_voltage_angles at 0x000002278EE70F40>, **kwargs)
functions.description: This function calculates and implements the rei or ward/xward network equivalents.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: The pandapower network including power flow results will not be changed during this function.

parameters.name: eq_type
parameters.description: type of the eqvalent network The following methods are available: - "rei": The idea of rei equivalent is to aggregate the power and current injection of the external buses to one or more fictitious radial, equivalent and independent (rei) nodes. There are three types of the rei-node in this routine, i.e. the reserved load, the reserved sgen and the reserved gen (also ext_grid). According to the demand, these elements (load, sgen and gen) are considered in the function "_create_net_zpbn" integrated or separately. - "ward": The ward-type equivalent represents the external network with some equivalent impedance, shunts and power injections at boundary buses. The equivalent power injections represent the power of the elements (load, sgen and gen), which are removed by the equivalent calculation. - "xward": The xward equivalent is an extended variation of the ward equivalent. Addition to the ward-representation, a fictitious PV node (generator) is added with zero active power injection at every boundary bus. The voltage of the PV node is set according to the boundary bus voltage. ward/xward has two mothods to develop an equivalent circuits, i.e. the injection method and the admittance method. In the admittance method, all the bus power injections in the external networks are converted into shunt admittance before network equivalent. That is the only difference between these two methods. With the help of the function "adapt_net", these methods are configurable.

parameters.name: boundary_buses
parameters.description: list of boundary bus indices, by which the original network are divided into two networks, i.e. an internal network and an external network.

parameters.name: internal_buses
parameters.description: list of bus indices, which are within the internal network. The program will add buses which are connected to this list of internal buses without passing boundary buses. If 'internal_buses' is an empty list or None, the whole grid is treated as external network.

parameters.name: return_internal
parameters.description: Reservation of the internal network If True, the internal network is reserved in the final equivalent network; otherwise only the external network is the output.

parameters.name: show_computing_time
parameters.description: show computing time of each step

parameters.name: ward_type
parameters.description: Type of ward and xward ward and xward proposed two mothods called the Ward Injection method and the Ward Admittance method to develop equivalent circuits. The only difference between these methods is that in the Ward Admittance method, all bus power in the external networks are converted into shunt admittances before network equivalent.

parameters.name: adapt_va_degree
parameters.description: if True, in add_ext_grids_to_boundaries(), the va_degree of the additional ext_grids (if needed) at the boundary buses will be increased or decreased to values that minimize the difference to the given res_bus.va_degree values.

parameters.name: calculate_voltage_angles
parameters.description: parameter passed to internal runpp() runs.

parameters.name: allow_net_change_for_convergence
parameters.description: if the net doesn't converge at the first internal power flow, which is in add_ext_grids_to_boundaries(), and this parameter is True, the code tests if changes to unusual impedance values solve the divergence issue.

return_info.description: **net_eq** - The equivalent network in pandapower format

functions.description: Class representing a generic time series controller for a specified element and variable. Control strategy: "No Control" -> updates values of specified elements according to timeseries input data. If ConstControl is used without timeseries input data, it will reset the controlled values to the initial values, preserving the initial net state. The timeseries values are written to net during time_step before the initial powerflow run and before other controllers' control_step. It is possible to set attributes of objects that are contained in a net table, e.g. attributes of other controllers. This can be helpful e.g. if a voltage setpoint of a transformer tap changer depends on the time step. An attribute of an object in the "object" column of a table (e.g. net.controller["object"] -> net.controller.object.at[0, "vm_set_pu"] can be set if the attribute is specified as "object.attribute" (e.g. "object.vm_set_pu").

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: element table ('sgen', 'load' etc.)

parameters.name: variable
parameters.description: variable ('p_mw', 'q_mvar', 'vm_pu', 'tap_pos', 'scaling' etc.) — use 'scaling' to apply multiplicative load profiles (most common for time series); use absolute variables like 'p_mw' only when data_source provides actual MW values, not scaling factors

parameters.name: element_index
parameters.description: IDs of the controlled elements

parameters.name: profile_name
parameters.description: The profile names of the elements in the data source

parameters.name: data_source
parameters.description: The data source that provides profile data

parameters.name: scale_factor
parameters.description: Scaling factor for time series input values

parameters.name: in_service
parameters.description: Indicates if the controller is currently in_service

parameters.name: recycle
parameters.description: Re-use of internal-data in a time series loop.

parameters.name: drop_same_existing_ctrl
parameters.description: Indicates if already existing controllers of the same type and with the same matching parameters (e.g. at same element) should be dropped

examples:
import pandapower as pp
import pandas as pd
from pandapower.timeseries import DFData, OutputWriter, run_timeseries
from pandapower.control import ConstControl
# Build a minimal 2-bus network
net = pp.create_empty_network()
b1 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.)
b2 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.)
pp.create_ext_grid(net, bus=b1)
pp.create_line(net, from_bus=b1, to_bus=b2, length_km=1.0, std_type='NAYY 4x50 SE')
load = pp.create_load(net, bus=b2, p_mw=1.0)
# Create scaling profiles (values 0.6–1.4 are multiplied with base load p_mw)
n_steps = 3
profiles = pd.DataFrame({'load': [0.8, 1.0, 1.2]})  # scaling factors
ds = DFData(profiles)
# Use variable='scaling' so profile values multiply the base p_mw
ConstControl(net, element='load', element_index=load, variable='scaling',
             data_source=ds, profile_name='load')
ow = OutputWriter(net, time_steps=range(n_steps))
run_timeseries(net, time_steps=range(n_steps), verbose=False)
# Access results: ow.output is a dict of DataFrames keyed by 'table.column'
result_at_t1 = ow.output['res_bus.vm_pu'].at[1, b2]  # timestep 1, bus b2

functions.name: SplineCharacteristic
functions.description: SplineCharacteristic interpolates the y-value(s) for the given x-value(s) according to a non-linear function. Internally the interpolator object interp1d from scipy.interpolate is used. By default, the function is quadratic, but the user can specify other methods (refer to the documentation of interp1d). The fill_value can be specified as "extrapolate" so that even x-values outside of the specified range can be used and yield y-values outside the specified y range. Alternatively, the behavior of Characteristic can be followed by providing a tuple for the fill value for x outside the specified range, refer to the documentation of interp1d for more details. We set the parameter bounds_error to False.

functions.name: run_timeseries
functions.description: Time Series main function. Runs a time series power flow simulation by iterating over time steps and calling controllers at each step. IMPORTANT: Do NOT pass output_writer as a keyword argument to this function — doing so uses the deprecated API and will raise a warning. Instead, create an OutputWriter by passing net as the first argument (e.g., ow = OutputWriter(net, output_path=...)), which automatically registers it with the network. Then call run_timeseries(net, time_steps=...) directly without any output_writer argument.

import pandapower as pp
import pandas as pd
from pandapower.timeseries import DFData, OutputWriter, run_timeseries
from pandapower.control import ConstControl
net = pp.create_empty_network()
b1 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.)
b2 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.)
pp.create_ext_grid(net, bus=b1)
pp.create_line(net, from_bus=b1, to_bus=b2, length_km=1.0, std_type='NAYY 4x50 SE')
load = pp.create_load(net, bus=b2, p_mw=1.0)
# Create scaling profiles for 3 time steps
profiles = pd.DataFrame({'load': [0.8, 1.0, 1.2]})  # multiplicative scaling
ds = DFData(profiles)
ConstControl(net, element='load', element_index=load, variable='scaling',
             data_source=ds, profile_name='load')
# OutputWriter automatically registers with the network; do NOT pass it to run_timeseries
ow = OutputWriter(net, time_steps=range(3))
run_timeseries(net, time_steps=range(3), verbose=False)
# Results are in ow.output, a dict of DataFrames keyed by 'table.column'
# DataFrame index = time step, columns = element indices
result = ow.output['res_bus.vm_pu'].at[2, b2]  # bus b2 voltage at time step 2
print(result)

parameters.description: pandapower net

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: index of the considered group

examples:
import pandapower as pp
net = pp.create_empty_network()
b1 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.0)
b2 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.0)
pp.create_ext_grid(net, bus=b1)
pp.create_line(net, from_bus=b1, to_bus=b2, length_km=1.0, std_type="NAYY 4x50 SE")
load = pp.create_load(net, bus=b2, p_mw=0.1, q_mvar=0.05)
group_id = pp.create_group(net, element_types=["load"], element_indices=[[load]], name="MyGroup")
pp.runpp(net)
q_mvar = pp.group_res_q_mvar(net, group_id)

functions.name: return_group_as_net
functions.description: Returns a pandapower net consisting of the members of this group.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: pandapower net

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: index of the considered group

parameters.name: keep_everything_else
parameters.description: Decides whether other data than element tables are kept, by default False

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Decides whether logging messages are triggered, by default True

return_info.description: ------- pandapowerNet pandapower net, only with elements that are members of the group

examples:
import pandapower as pp
net = pp.create_empty_network()
b1 = pp.create_bus(net, vn_kv=20.0)
load = pp.create_load(net, bus=b1, p_mw=0.1)
group_id = pp.create_group(net, element_types=["load"], element_indices=[[load]], name="MyGroup")
group_net = pp.return_group_as_net(net, group_id)

functions.name: _add_dcline_gens
functions.description: Converts each DC line in a pandapower network into equivalent generator entries at the from and to buses, accounting for active power direction, losses, voltage setpoints, reactive power limits, and in-service status.

parameters.name: net
parameters.description: pandapower network containing a dcline table to be converted into generator entries

return_info.description: None; equivalent generator entries are added to the input network in place
